newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU puts off discussion on new media law.
newsitem.headline: EU puts off discussion on new media law.

text.p: The European Commission postponed on Wednesday a discussion on a controversial plan for a new media law, aimed at curbing domination of the media by a handful of industry moguls.
Mario Monti, the Commissioner responsible for the EU market, said the the EU executive had simply run out of time at its weekly meeting.
"A decision was taken...to postpone the item till next week," he told a news conference.

With a majority of Commissioners in favour of the plan, the executive had been expected to agree in principle to put the brakes on media expansion when a company reaches a certain audience share, leaving agreement on the fine details until later.

The proposal for an EU directive to protect media pluralism, which has European publishers up in arms, responds to strong demands from the European Parliament for EU legislation to protect pluralism and democracy which it sees as being threatened by media moguls like Silvio Berlusconi and Rupert Murdoch.

Berlusconi is a major media figure in Italy, while Murdoch operates one of the world's biggest broadcast and press groups with interests in many markets, including Europe, the United States, Asia and Australia.
European groups, arguing that EU legislation would hinder their ability to adapt and compete in a fast changing media world, have lobbied furiously against the plan.
